## Describe the response you need

The adjacent [construction fixture](fixtures/primitive_resonator.py) only
repeats lesson 1's Plan and handles. `CircuitRun` owns execution and
`run.original` is its zero-reduction [network view](../../docs/concepts/compilation-coordinates-and-network-views.qmd#network-view-lineage).
Because this Plan has one logical Port, the original view already means its
complete one-Port response. `DirectSolveSpec` requests S/Y/Z on an explicit
frequency grid; it does not require a named trace.

The workspace stores exact request receipts and artifacts. It is not a
mutable “latest result” directory, and independent requests may coexist in it.

```{python}
#| id: prepare-direct-response
from fixtures.primitive_resonator import build_primitive_resonator
from scnsim import (
    CircuitRun,
    DirectSolveSpec,
    units as u,
)

fixture = build_primitive_resonator()
run = CircuitRun(plan=fixture.plan, workspace="workspaces/primitive-course")
direct_spec = DirectSolveSpec(
    frequencies=[5.5, 6.0, 6.5, 7.0] * u.GHz,
)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Optional: inspect before solving" appearance="simple"}
`run.explain()` returns an `ExplanationResult` from deterministic preflight
without solving or writing a workspace Result. Use it when you want to inspect
the resolved request first.

```python
run.explain(run.original, direct_spec).show()
```
:::

## Solve and inspect the response

`run.solve()` materializes a typed `DirectSolveResult`; it does not store a
mutable current Result on the Run. `direct.s`, `direct.y`, and `direct.z`
describe the same selected network in three matrix families. `show()` only
presents materialized data and never solves again.

```{python}
#| id: solve-direct-response
direct = run.solve(run.original, direct_spec)
direct.s.show(magnitude="db")
direct.y.view
direct.z.view
```
